issues.title: [Bug][GLM-5.2-W4A8C8][co-located] Stochastic async MTP enters a parser-before periodic raw-token loop
issues.body:
## Why this is a separate report

This is an independent **two-node co-located** reproduction, not P/D disaggregation. It is related to #14463 and #14656, but adds two isolation results that those issue bodies do not contain:

1. the failure reproduces through the vLLM OpenAI-compatible endpoint directly, bypassing the agent harness, LiteLLM, and the API gateway;
2. `return_token_ids=true` proves that the periodic loop already exists in the engine's raw output token IDs before GLM tool parsing.

The symptom eventually becomes repeated or unterminated `tool_calls[].function.arguments`, but the parser is downstream of the first observed corruption in this case.

## Impact

In a production-style agent request, approximately 0.9%-1.0% of default-sampling requests entered a long-running periodic token loop. They continued returning HTTP 200 SSE chunks until a 300-second client protection timeout, with no terminal `finish_reason`, usage chunk, or `[DONE]`. If the incomplete tool call is persisted and sent back in a later turn, downstream JSON parsing reports `Unterminated string` and returns HTTP 400.

## Reproduction statistics

All runs used the same request shape and called the serving endpoint directly:

| Arm | Result |
|---|---:|
| default model sampling, concurrency 4 | 991/1000 completed; 9/1000 timed out at 300 s |
| independent default-sampling repeat, concurrency 4 | 297/300 completed; 3/300 timed out at 300 s |
| `temperature=0`, concurrency 4 | 300/300 completed; 0/300 observed timeouts |

The zero failures in 300 greedy requests are evidence that stochastic sampling is a trigger/risk factor; they are not claimed as proof of a complete fix.

The request did **not** set `tool_choice`, `strict`, or `temperature`. It therefore used auto tool choice and the model's default generation configuration (`temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`).

Non-sensitive request shape:

```text
OpenAI Chat Completions
stream=true
about 50,190 prompt tokens after template application
36 messages
85 function tool schemas
max_completion_tokens=128,000 (an upper bound, not a fixed requested output length)
stream_options.include_usage=true
return_token_ids=true for the evidence run
concurrency=4
per-request protection timeout=300 seconds
```

## Parser-before raw-token evidence

All three failures in the 300-request evidence run had low-diversity periodic repetition in raw `output.token_ids` before parser processing. The three token-stream hashes and best periods were different, so this is not one SSE response duplicated by the client or proxy.

| Request | Raw engine token evidence | Token-stream SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| 44 | best period 13 over the last 8192 tokens; 74.61% agreement | `a5f86d630332741d00746281a50594bd4d07f4496f63f08cd5201c45419a096b` |
| 82 | exact period 768 over a 6144-token tail; 5376/5376 comparable tokens match | `e1df762935c36e64f1383e0bfba62c9f86683e3d27a45d0b8c3a69bd3fee754d` |
| 142 | exact period 8 over the last 8192 tokens; 8184/8184 comparable tokens match | `eb9cd9c12bffa1ebe41dba9c4294bf1c9749082c67494a045314cb9d5cd13b5b` |

After those raw-token loops begin, the parser converts the repeated GLM tool markup into repeated/unclosed arguments. For request 82, the parsed argument tail also repeats exactly (period 1248 characters) and ends with `Unterminated string`. Request 142 independently produces a different repeated argument period and the same incomplete-JSON class.

## Environment

```text
Hardware: two Atlas 800 A3 hosts, 16 Ascend910 devices visible per host
Deployment: co-located serving, not P/D disaggregation
Parallelism: DP4 / TP8 / DCP8 / PCP1 / PP1, EP enabled
Model: GLM-5.2-W4A8C8, GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM
Speculative decode: deepseek_mtp, num_speculative_tokens=3
KV connector: AscendStoreConnector, kv_role=kv_both, MemCache backend
Context: max-model-len=1,024,000
Tool parser: glm47
Reasoning parser: glm45
CANN: 9.1.0, innerversion V100R001C11SPC001B243
PyTorch: 2.10.0+cpu
torch-npu: 2.10.0.post4
vLLM: 0.23.0, commit 0fc695fc6d1d82e9a5ac6835ac8e4e1c83703665
vLLM-Ascend: 0.23.0, commit 5cb98caaadeff42b5b62b996e34bb2aaa29d20fd
transformers: 5.5.4
```

Immutable official base image:

```text
quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend@sha256:382b012420854ba2d8b3b78897d9216742f27948345e503a01644ebbdd706ce6
```

The derivative image, Dockerfile, and applied parser backports are documented here:

https://gist.github.com/ZhengDeL/0b63136e32a5e573109aa4e1afb18d57

Complete sanitized host commands, image provenance, package versions, model fingerprints, and source hashes were already posted here:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/14463#issuecomment-5345634154

## Fix/version audit already performed

- vLLM #45915 and #46351 are present in the tested image. They improve GLM streaming parsing, but the parser-before token loop still reproduces.
- vLLM-Ascend #13865 is present byte-for-byte in both serving images. The issue still reproduces, so the async accepted-token snapshot fix is insufficient by itself.
- vLLM #47512 / issue #47504 cover `tool_choice=required`; this request uses auto tool choice and does not set `tool_choice`.
- vLLM #52805 covers speculative grammar advancement after structural-tag termination. This request has neither `strict` nor required/named tool choice, so it does not build that constrained structural-tag path.
- vLLM-Ascend #13766 fixes an always-accepting rejection sampler in ModelRunner V2 on v0.26+. The tested v0.23 path is ModelRunner V1 and uses generated uniform probabilities, not the hardcoded `u=0.0` code fixed there.
- vLLM-Ascend #14536 is specific to P/D decode nodes with `enable_sparse_sfa_c8`; this reproduction is co-located and uses `enable_sparse_li_c8` without `enable_sparse_sfa_c8`.
- vLLM-Ascend #14451 may be relevant to GLM-5.2 MTP shared-index handling on the v0.26rc line, but it is still a draft with no end-to-end validation for this failure mode.
- As of 2026-08-20, the latest published vLLM-Ascend release is v0.23.0. Main/v0.26rc contains additional candidate fixes, but no released or merged change claims to fix this parser-before periodic raw-token loop.

## Questions for maintainers

1. Which component should own the next isolation step: GLM hybrid/MTP state, DCP/distributed decode state, W4A8C8 numerical behavior, or KV reuse?
2. Is there an exact main/release-branch commit that is expected to fix this raw-token loop, rather than only malformed parser output?
3. Is #14451 applicable to in-model `deepseek_mtp` under this DP4/TP8/DCP8 topology, and if so, which commit should be tested?
4. Could the diagnostic facilities in #12209 (MTP acceptance/token-repeat/logprob/tensor dump) be provided as a testable branch or minimal patch for this case?
5. We can run controlled A/B tests on isolated validation instances with raw token capture: MTP on/off, DCP on/off, async path on/off, MemCache on/off, and W4A8C8 versus W8A8C8/BF16. Please advise the preferred order and any additional tensors/counters to capture.

This is affecting a production tool-calling workload. We would appreciate an owner and priority triage. The customer payload cannot be posted publicly, but a complete evidence archive can be shared privately with maintainers if needed.

issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add an offline four-NPU functional gate for non-Flash GLM5.x DSA models, following `test_kimi_k3.py`. The test constructs a temporary configuration, initializes dummy BF16 weights, and supplies token IDs directly. No checkpoint, tokenizer download, dataset, or numerical/performance baseline is required.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Stage 2 of #15877 adds six real Mooncake PD contracts in five E2E files. This revision is based on the same stable compatibility pair as #15878:

- vLLM v0.28.0: `2cf0a6915ce544dc493a0990f2ea38d81601128a`
- vllm-ascend main: `660c4582aa580ce98edc9b681bb6ff6d03153575`

The PR contains only E2E tests, their shared helpers/material tooling, and focused CPU tests for those helpers. It contains no production change to `mooncake_connector.py`, `mooncake_hybrid_connector.py`, or any other file under `vllm_ascend/`.

| Model | Material | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-8B | Full BF16 | Basic and prefix with KV pooling; exact tokens; unavailable-transfer failure and recovery |
| K3 | 4 text layers, 16 experts, W4A8 | Hybrid KDA/MLA, TP2/EP, prefix/chunked/Graph, exact tokens |
| DSV4 | 4 layers, W8A8_DYNAMIC | `MooncakeHybridConnector`, compression 0/0/4/128, 4096-token page boundaries |
| GLM5.2 | 7 layers, W8A8 | Full/shared indexers, TP2/EP, KV pooling, 2048-token indexer boundary |
| MiniMax-M3 | 5 text layers, W8A8_DYNAMIC | Dense/sparse attention, TP2/EP, prefix/Graph, exact tokens |

Every case requires a successful nonempty correlated KV transfer, decoder Graph replay, output agreement with an independently started colocated reference, and bounded cleanup of owned processes. Prefix cases clear or disable D's local cache before the correlated request. Direct-connector cases retain P's local prefix; the Qwen prefix and GLM pooling cases additionally clear P's local cache and require a real pool load. The correlated request extends the warmed prefix by one known token so it exercises partial-prefix transfer rather than a full local hit. Missing materials, startup failures, and recompute fallback fail the test.

K3 and DSV4 align the colocated reference with the stateful PD boundary by processing all but the final known input token on prefill and forcing only that token before generating ten unconstrained answer tokens. Reduced GLM/DSV4 materials disable MTP because layer pruning does not preserve full-model draft acceptance. DSV4 uses `MooncakeHybridConnector` as required by its mixed cache layout.

GLM uses the existing Ascend top-five precision limits: maximum logprob delta below 1.0, mean below 0.15, and mutual top-five greedy membership. DSV4 retains mutual top-five greedy membership but uses explicit 2.0/0.3 limits for its lossy C128-compressed Hybrid pages; repeated A3 runs measured 1.41/0.24 and 1.28/0.26. Qwen/K3/MiniMax require exact generated token equality.

Qwen prefix and GLM5.2 combine their PD connector with `AscendStoreConnector` through `MultiConnector`. They reuse the existing single-node pool manager to start and stop an isolated `mooncake_master`, contribute 1 GB per rank through A3 fabric memory, and use `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`. After warming the pool, both P and D local prefix caches are reset. The correlated request must allocate a positive number of external tokens with zero P-local cached tokens and complete a nonempty backend get, then perform the original P-to-D transfer and output comparison. D's pool lookup is disabled so Store cannot bypass the PD path. The `kv_pool` coverage tag is registered separately from embedding-model `pooling`.

### Failure handling

The E2E assertions remain active while validating the stable pair. If a failure comes from an invalid or unnecessarily strict test assumption, this PR updates that assumption. A confirmed production defect is tracked in a separate issue and the affected case may be skipped with the issue URL as its reason; production connector fixes are outside this PR.

The earlier repository-wide mypy failure at `vllm_ascend/xlite/xlite.py:664` is tracked independently in #16658. This revision passes the latest GitHub pre-commit job, including mypy, without a production change in this PR.

### Validation

- Stable-pair helper tests: `VLLM_VERSION=0.28.0 PYTHONPATH=$VLLM_V028_ROOT uv run pytest -q tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/test_pd_http.py tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/test_pd_materials.py tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/test_pd_output.py tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/test_pd_reference.py tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/test_pd_pool.py` — **34 passed**.
- Current-main compatibility helper tests with vLLM `6fbb00b18874e27ba7d7adc0a3b8e93fee763ab1` — **34 passed**.
- Local pre-commit on all modified files — all executed hooks passed. The local gitleaks hook was skipped because the macOS environment lacks the required binary; GitHub CI runs that check.
- Before adding pooling, commit `f12c48ca` passed all six A3 stable-pair E2E contracts, logical devices 12-15 (Qwen uses 12-13): Qwen basic, Qwen prefix, K3, DSV4, GLM5.2, and MiniMax-M3. Each run observed real KV transfer and Graph replay.
- Pooling revision `d6e4773e`, same stable pair on A3 165: **2 passed**, Qwen prefix in 147.23s (devices 12-13), GLM5.2 in 249.54s (devices 12-15). Both prove Pool -> P -> D after local-cache reset, retain Graph replay and output checks, and clean up owned servers/master. Qwen loads 1536 tokens / 12 keys; GLM loads 3072 tokens / 24 keys per TP rank. GLM maximum logprob delta across checks is 0.271689 and maximum mean delta is 0.043011.
- [GitHub CI for commit `d6e4773e`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35174153885): DCO and pre-commit (including gitleaks and mypy on Python 3.10/3.11/3.12) passed. CPU UT passed: **4918 passed, 38 skipped**. issues.title: [RFC]: Hybrid dense/sparse attention routing for GLM-5.3-Flash
issues.body:
### Motivation. GLM-5.3-Flash uses KeyPool-based selection and sparse MLA attention. When a query’s complete causal history fits within the selection budget, all valid historical tokens are selected, making indexer scoring unnecessary. This opportunity also exists inside longer prefills. With an uncached 8K prompt and a 2K selection budget, the first 2K query rows are full-visible while later rows require sparse selection. This RFC proposes request-aware indexer bypass and hybrid dense/sparse attention routing for GLM-5.3-Flash on Ascend. The implementation should establish the benefit of each component independently. Refs #15665. ### Proposed Change. **Before and after** ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph before["Before: all query rows follow the same path"] direction TB B0["All query rows"] --> B1["KeyPool, tail and KV-cache updates"] B1 --> B2["Indexer query / head-weight projections
Scoring + TopK for all rows"] B2 --> B3["SFA for all rows"] B3 --> B4["Attention output"] end subgraph after["Proposed: request-aware hybrid routing"] direction TB A0["All query rows"] --> A1["KeyPool, tail and KV-cache updates
Preserved for all required tokens"] A1 --> A2["Plan query ranges per request"] A2 -->|"Full-visible rows"| A3["Bypass indexer projections, scoring and TopK
Direct causal indices where needed"] A2 -->|"Selective rows"| A4["Indexer query / head-weight projections
Scoring + TopK over complete causal key history"] A3 --> A5{"Dense path supported
and profitable?"} A5 -->|"Yes"| A6["Dense MLA / FIA"] A5 -->|"No"| A7["SFA"] A4 --> A7 A6 --> A8["Restore common output format
and original query order"] A7 --> A8 A8 --> A9["Attention output"] end ``` For an uncached 8K prompt with a 2K selection budget, the proposed plan routes the first 2K query rows through the full-visible branch and the remaining 6K through sparse selection. Each query retains its complete causal key history. Cache maintenance still covers all required tokens. The diagram shows the target hybrid flow. Indexer bypass is first validated with SFA for both branches; dense routing is enabled only when supported and profitable. **1. Plan query ranges** For selection budget `K`, cached context length `C` and current query length `Q`, initially use the conservative full-visible prefix: ```text full_visible_rows = min(Q, max(0, K - C)) ``` Build the plan from trustworthy metadata, preserving request boundaries, causal positions and original query order. Include cached prefixes and speculative positions without introducing device-to-host synchronization. **2. Bypass redundant indexer work** Continue KeyPool construction, compressor-tail updates and cache writes for the complete required input. Skip indexer query projection, head-weight projection, scoring and TopK for full-visible rows. Generate their valid causal indices directly, and run normal selection for the remaining rows. Selection metadata must describe the selected query ranges without truncating their key history. Preserve existing index-buffer conventions and downstream shared-index consumers. First validate this change with the existing SFA consumer to isolate indexer savings. **3. Add hybrid attention routing** Evaluate a compatible dense MLA/FIA path for full-visible rows while retaining SFA for selective rows. Pack eligible ranges where profitable, then restore results to the same output representation and original row order. Admission must account for NoPE geometry, cache format, projection costs, KV gathering or dequantization, workspace and result-restoration overhead. Retain normal SFA when the alternative is unsupported or more expensive. For larger prefills, separately evaluate masked-MHA execution that preserves model-defined sparse selection. Introduce it only after confirming Ascend operator support, bounded workspace and end-to-end benefit. **4. Validate correctness and profitability** Cover selection-budget and pool/tail boundaries, ragged batches, cached-prefix continuation, chunked prefill, speculative positions and transitions between routes. Compare selected-token sets, attention outputs, cache state and end-to-end generation against normal selection and SFA. Include numerical tolerances, complete natural-stop answers, task accuracy and speculative acceptance behavior. Benchmark indexer bypass and attention routing separately. Report indexer latency, attention latency, TTFT, throughput and peak workspace, including all planning and data-movement costs. Use short, 8K and longer inputs with matched cache policies. Determine routing thresholds from Ascend measurements rather than assuming that every full-visible range benefits from dense execution. ### Feedback Period. At least one week. Feedback is requested on query-range ownership, suitable Ascend attention primitives and profitability criteria. ### Any Other Things. The initial target is GLM-5.3-Flash on MRV2. Reuse existing cache, indexer and attention interfaces where practical. No new environment variable is proposed.

issues.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```text
vLLM version: v0.30.0
vLLM Ascend version: 0.30.0rc1 + PR #19309
Hardware: Atlas 910B (8 NPU), CANN 9.2.0
Model: GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 (W8A8 quantized, ascend quant)

```

</details>


### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Reproduction

```bash
# Only the MTP block changes between the three runs; everything else is identical.
vllm serve /home/ma-user/work/GLM/GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8-261013 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --seed 1024 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --served-model-name GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-model-len 204800 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --async-scheduling \
  --safetensors-load-strategy 'prefetch' \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,4,8,16,32,64,96,128]}' \
  --additional-config '{
    "scheduler_config": {"enable_balance_scheduling": true},
    "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true,
    "enable_mlapo": true,
    "enable_flashcomm1": false,
    "enable_fused_mc2": true,
    "weight_nz_mode": 1,
    "enable_dsa_cp": false
  }' \
  --speculative-config '{
    "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
    "method": "deepseek_mtp",
    "enforce_eager": true
  }' \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45
```

Workload: `ais_bench` `default_perf`, fixed input length × fixed output length, `request_rate=0.25 req/s`, 36 jobs (input length 32k/64k/128k/200k × 1k output × `prefix_cache` off/on × bs 1/2/4/8/16/32).

### Expected behavior

`num_speculative_tokens=3` (`ns=3`) should give a higher mean acceptance length than `ns=1`, since up to 3 draft tokens can be accepted per step. At minimum, per-position acceptance should decay smoothly (e.g. 0.85 → 0.70 → 0.55), which never produces a *worse* result than a single draft token.

### Actual behavior

`ns=3` is dramatically worse than `ns=1` on the same TP4×PP2 layout, and `ns=3` produces a pathological 3rd position.

The table below is derived from vLLM's own serve-side `SpecDecoding metrics` log lines (`metrics.py:120`), aggregated per benchmark job by summing `Accepted`/`Drafted` over the job's time window. It is not reverse-engineered from client timings.

| Config | Avg draft acceptance rate (all positions) | Per-position acceptance (mean over 36 jobs) | Mean acceptance length (MAL) | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MRV1 + TP4×PP2 + MTP, ns=3, graphs + async | **36.7%** | **62.0% / 29.8% / 18.4%** | 0.367 | ❌ Abnormal acceptance rate |
| MRV1 + TP4×PP2 + MTP, ns=1, graphs + async | 88.5% | 88.5% (single pos) | 0.885 → MAL 1.83 | ✅ correct |
| TP8 + MTP, ns=3, graphs + async | 65.3% | 84.6% / 65.0% / 46.3% | 0.653 → MAL 2.10 | ✅ correct |

Key observations:

**1. TP8 with identical `ns=3` and identical workload recovers 65.3% / 84.6-65.0-46.3%.**

TP8 and TP4×PP2 use the same model, same `ns=3`, same `deepseek_mtp`, same `enforce_eager: true`, same cudagraph config, same batch sizes. The only structural difference is TP4×PP2 (pipeline-parallel depth 2, and the MTP drafter replicated over PP stages) vs TP8 (PP=1). That isolates the defect to the **PP + MTP combination**, not to GLM-5.3's MTP weights and not to `ns=3` in general.

Per-position means, TP4×PP2 `ns=3` vs TP8 `ns=3`:

| Draft position | TP4×PP2 | TP8 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pos1 | 62.0% | 84.6% |
| pos2 | 29.8% | 65.0% |
| pos3 | 18.4% | 46.3% |

Position 1 alone loses 22.6 points. Position 1 is produced by the *first* forward of the MTP layer from the same hidden state and does not depend on the previous draft token, so a plain "later positions decay" explanation cannot account for pos1 regressing at all. Something in the drafter's input/anchor state under PP2 appears to be wrong or stale.

**2. Position 3 degenerates to exactly 0.000 acceptance in 16.4% of samples on PP2 — this is not a decay curve.**

Scanning all `SpecDecoding metrics` lines in the TP4×PP2 `ns=3` serve log (1478 samples) and the TP8 `ns=3` serve log (1233 samples):

| Metric | TP4×PP2 `ns=3` | TP8 `ns=3` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Samples with pos3 == exactly `0.000` | **243 / 1478 (16.4%)** | 31 / 1233 (2.5%) |
| Samples with pos3 < 0.10 | 42.3% | 2.8% |
| Samples with pos2 < 0.10 | 19.1% | 1.1% |
| pos3 mean / median | 0.186 / 0.138 | 0.465 / 0.476 |

An acceptance rate of *exactly* zero means every single drafted token at that position was rejected for the whole 10 s metrics window. Representative consecutive samples from the TP4×PP2 `ns=3` log during a long-context, bs=1 job:

```
SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.28, Accepted: 38, Drafted: 414,
  Per-position acceptance rate: 0.261, 0.014, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 9.2%
SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.17, Accepted: 32, Drafted: 561,
  Per-position acceptance rate: 0.166, 0.005, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 5.7%
SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.53, Accepted: 105, Drafted: 594,
  Per-position acceptance rate: 0.525, 0.005, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 17.7%
SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.66, Accepted: 129, Drafted: 588,
  Per-position acceptance rate: 0.653, 0.005, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 21.9%
```

issues.title: [Bug]: MemCache layerwise allocates ~4× the KV payload for GLM-5.3-Flash with PP=1
issues.body:
## Your current environment

- Ascend A3, GLM-5.3-Flash-W8A8, BF16 KV (`--kv-cache-dtype auto`)
- vLLM 0.32.0, vLLM Ascend [d96c01e5c2](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/d96c01e5c2266d6df061311e8966e096bc542f68), using the unmodified base image
- P/D disaggregation with TP8 on each side, PP=1, PCP=1, DCP=1, MTP with 3 draft tokens, `--mamba-cache-mode align`
- `MultiConnector` with `MooncakeConnectorV2` for P/D transfer and `AscendStoreConnector` with `{"backend":"memcache","use_layerwise":true}` for P-side prefix caching. The MemCache consumer has `consumer_is_to_load=false` and `consumer_is_to_put=false`.
- MemCache DRAM pool with 16 × 10 GiB. P uses `--enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-model-len 262144`. The engine selects 640-token cache blocks.

## Describe the bug

Start with an empty pool and send one cold 131,072-token text prompt with `max_tokens=1`. Once the prompt's full blocks have been saved, the MemCache audit reports **1,020 live keys, 25.702 GiB used, and zero evictions**. The tensors written into those objects account for approximately **6.421 GiB**. Roughly 75% of the allocated space is unused within the objects. The same run reached 131.535 GiB used before eviction began during the following write.

The P worker reports 12 physical layers in the MLA/indexer group (including MTP) and 12, 11, and 11 layers in the three KDA groups. The allocator log reports object sizes of 32,030,720 and 25,812,992 bytes. These sizes and the key count reconstruct the first audit sample:

| Object type | Count | Allocated bytes per object | Allocated GiB | Payload GiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MLA KV + compressed indexer | 204 full blocks, one shared copy across TP | 696,320 bytes/layer × 46 | 6.086 | 1.588 |
| KDA checkpoints | 34 checkpoints × 3 groups × 8 TP shards = 816 | 561,152 bytes/layer × 46 | 19.617 | 4.833 |
| Total | 1,020 | | 25.702 | 6.421 |

The checkpoint count follows from 204 full blocks and 6 aligned blocks per prefill chunk. The payload column counts all observed checkpoints and uses the actual layer count for each cache group.

## Code path

The [MemCache layerwise save path](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/d96c01e5c2266d6df061311e8966e096bc542f68/vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/layerwise/pool_worker.py#L1276-L1278) uses `_global_group_alloc_size(group_id)` for `batch_alloc`. In [the tested revision](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/d96c01e5c2266d6df061311e8966e096bc542f68/vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/pool_worker.py#L615-L639), the helper sizes each group's region using the full model layer span, even with PP=1 and a zero PP byte offset. The [same sizing formula is present on main](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/89eb8a5e7a76d085b453a1aeadb6883e12d5ea2d/vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/pool_worker.py#L557-L580). The hardware measurement is from the pinned base image.

## Pipeline-parallel layout

[PR #16412](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16412) added the MemCache `@pp{rank}` key component for PP > 1 and merged at 02:26 UTC on 2026-09-15. [PR #16208](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16208) added global layer addressing and the model-wide GVA allocation formula and merged at 03:44 UTC the same day.

In the tested revision, MemCache full-block keys contain the group ID and, for PP > 1, the stage rank. The GVA copy path still adds the stage's global byte offset. Shrinking allocations alone under PP could put those copies outside the object. A compact PP layout would have to update the writer and reader offsets together. With stage-qualified keys, each stage could store its own group data starting at byte zero. Cross-topology reads would need to resolve the writer's stage and group-local offset for each layer. DCP shard alignment must also be preserved.

For the immediate PP=1, DCP=1 case, MLA/indexer and KDA objects already use group-local copy offsets starting at zero. The last copied byte is bounded by `sum(group_block_len[group_id])`, so the expected allocation reduction needs no key or transfer-address change in that topology.

## Expected behavior

For PP=1 and DCP=1, size each MemCache GVA object to the bytes stored for that cache group, with any alignment the backend requires. Keep allocation, write, and read offsets consistent. A regression test should cover a hybrid MLA/KDA layout with MTP and verify that the PP shared-region and DCP shard layouts still work.

Related design discussion: #12234.

## Local validation of compact allocation

A temporary patch used `sum(group_block_len[group_id])` for MemCache objects when PP=1 and DCP=1, with the same keys and transfer offsets. The targeted CPU/mock suites passed (161 tests). On the same A3 comparator, the 8-prefix cold prime completed 8/8 requests. Meta recorded 8,160 live keys, 55,153,000,448 DRAM bytes (51.365 GiB, or 6.421 GiB per prefix on average), and zero evictions. The P external prefix hit counter increased by 368,640 tokens during the first three subsequent warmup requests.

The temporary change keeps the existing PP and DCP allocation paths. The full throughput sweep is still running.

issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

GLM DFlash2 selects device-length CANN FlashAttn only when the draft enforces eager execution. Enabling draft ACL graphs therefore falls back to FIA, whose metadata builder materializes exact device sequence lengths as Python lists and updates attention tasks on the host.

Allow eligible 950DT GLM DFlash2 drafts to use FlashAttn in both eager and graph modes. Length preparation and tiling remain inside graph capture. Compatible layers in the same attention group share producers through the existing `UpdatableGraph.get_capture_resource()` mechanism, keyed by metadata identity, token count and attention geometry. The DFlash capture path records one query forward per graph, so graph ownership provides the required cache lifetime without an additional context manager or forward callback wrapper. Warmup caches and independent graphs remain isolated. Replay executes the captured producers against persistent, rejection-corrected device buffers without FIA task updates.

The branch is based on the merged #21114 implementation. The obsolete PP embedding reload/sharing overrides from the earlier version of that PR are no longer included. This PR makes no additional changes to `qwen3_dspark.py`, `qwen3_dflash2.py`, or the DFlash model-loading override; the merged target-constructor fix and normal checkpoint-loading path are used unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Supported GLM (`glm_moe_dsa`) targets with `DFlash2DraftModel` can use device-length FlashAttn for full-graph drafts on 950DT Products without setting the draft's `enforce_eager` to true. Existing hardware, dtype, head-size and attention-feature fallback guards remain in place. The guide and release-note fragment document this scope.

The change reduces repeated captured metadata work. Latest serving measurements show a long-output single-concurrency TPOT improvement and a short-output TPOT regression. Concurrent long-input serving and full GSM8K validation failed in this run; no general performance or full-model accuracy claim is made.

issues.title: [Performance][GLM] Reuse device offsets for short-prefill recurrent KDA
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

A prefix-cache hit can leave a GLM-5.3-Flash request with only a few tokens to prefill. The prefill wrapper currently sends these tokens through chunk KDA, including its preparation work. For example, a four-token remainder takes the chunk path even though the builder already provides device sequence offsets suitable for recurrent KDA.

This PR routes eligible short prefills through the existing recurrent primitive and reuses `metadata.prefill_query_start_loc`. The layer passes the existing device tensor directly, avoiding a new offsets tensor or host upload. In the recorded A3 wrapper benchmark, four-token latency decreases from **545.91 μs to 308.35 μs**.

| Prefill input | Selected path |
| --- | --- |
| Device offsets available, no empty-segment compaction, 1–8 physical token rows | Recurrent KDA |
| Missing device offsets, compacted input, or other tensor lengths | Chunk KDA |

The length check uses `q.shape[1]`: total physical rows, including padding. Bounding this value to eight also bounds every logical sequence to eight tokens, matching the `MAX_MTP=8` recurrent-kernel contract used for this implementation. Compacted inputs retain chunk KDA because their filtered state rows no longer align with the original device offsets.

State ownership follows the existing prefill contract:

- Gather each request's initial state into scratch, with zero state for cold requests.
- Pass raw beta with `beta_is_preprocessed=False`; the recurrent primitive applies beta preprocessing and updates scratch in place.
- Scatter the final states back to the selected slots and zero output rows beyond the last valid offset.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Eligible short GLM-5.3-Flash prefills use recurrent KDA by default, with no new configuration. This changes the short-prefill stage; decode and the chunk fallback keep their existing dispatch. The release note is included in `release_notes/fragments/20822.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Current-commit CI

Head: [`0743f662f26c3aed0ede6f6dc09ba8673ca91792`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/0743f662f26c3aed0ede6f6dc09ba8673ca91792).

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Pre-commit | Passed |
| CPU UT with vLLM `v0.32.0` | Passed |
| CPU UT with vLLM `24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58` | Passed |
| Device test jobs | Skipped; test selection pending |
| `ci-gate` | Failed; device test selection remains outstanding |

[CI run and job results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/41666688341).

The added CPU tests check the 4/8/9-row routing boundary, compacted batches, device-offset object identity, raw-beta dispatch, initial-state gathering, selected-slot writeback, and zeroed padding. The dispatch test verifies that the model layer passes `prefill_query_start_loc` to the wrapper.

#### Current-commit common-reference precision — 2026-11-05

On Ascend 910C/A3 with CANN 9.2.1, PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu and torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, both dispatch paths were compared against the same CPU FP64 recurrent reference. The reference was cross-checked with the FLA-NPU recurrent CPU golden. Inputs use H16/K128/V128, BF16 q/k/v/gate/beta and FP32 state, with frozen CPU-generated inputs shared by both paths.

| Input | Chunk state max absolute error | Recurrent state max absolute error | Recurrent output / state |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 2 tokens | 4.0235370398e−4 | 3.3527612686e−8 | Pass / Pass |
| 4 tokens | 2.8571486473e−4 | 2.9802322388e−8 | Pass / Pass |
| 8 tokens | 3.8366019726e−4 | 2.6077032089e−8 | Pass / Pass |
| Packed 3+4 tokens, padded to 8 | 4.3662637472e−4 | 3.3527612686e−8 | Pass / Pass |

Recurrent output and state pass in all four cases; every recurrent state element meets the tolerance. Chunk outputs pass in all four cases, while chunk state element pass rates are 89.24%–92.27%, below the 99% requirement. In this comparison, recurrent state is closer to the common reference. Unselected state slots, cold-state initialization and zeroed recurrent padding also pass their checks.

The standalone comparison uses the unchanged ATK 26.9.8 `mixed_tolerance_bm` defaults: FP32 state rtol=9.77e−4, atol=1.53e−5; BF16 output rtol=atol=1.56e−2; at least 99% matching elements, plus the standard absolute-error/32-ULP condition. This is a focused wrapper check using those criteria, rather than a full ATK job.

<details>
<summary>Common-reference experiment setup</summary>

- Seed: `42 + physical_token_rows`. Generate q/k/v as CPU Gaussian tensors scaled by 0.1 and cast to BF16; raw gate and beta as BF16 Gaussian tensors; `A_log` and `dt_bias` zero; five FP32 state slots initialized from Gaussian values scaled by 0.01.
- Dense cases use state slot 1. Packed lengths 3/4 use slots 3/1, with an existing state for the first sequence and a cold state for the second.
- Invoke the current-head prefill wrapper with device offsets for recurrent, and with offsets omitted to select the existing chunk branch. The packed chunk comparison receives the seven valid rows; recurrent receives eight physical rows with one padding row. Compare valid outputs and selected states.
- The FP64 reference applies q/k L2 normalization with epsilon 1e−6, bounded gate `-5 * sigmoid(exp(A_log) * (raw_gate + dt_bias))`, beta sigmoid, and the recurrent state update. Round the reference to FP32 for comparison.
- The four cases execute once per path; no model weights or performance sweep are involved.

</details>

#### A3 device experiments — 2026-11-03

These experiments compared Ascend base `4946dab8a957e9670e51ecb380c574c5343f6c95` with the short-prefill candidate on that base, using vLLM `24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58`. They exercise the 1–8-row, non-compacted dispatch retained in this PR. Current-head hosted checks are listed separately above.

Environment: Ascend 910C/A3, CANN 9.2.1, driver 25.5.0, PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, and the installed FLA-NPU A3 Stable-ABI runtime. The experiment did not record a verifiable FLA-NPU package revision. Inputs use H16/D128, BF16 tensors and FP32 state.

| Physical token rows | Original chunk wrapper | Candidate wrapper |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2 | 626.45 μs | 350.15 μs |
| 4 | 545.91 μs | 308.35 μs |
| 8 | 474.64 μs | 267.48 μs |
| 9, chunk fallback | 474.04 μs | 475.59 μs |
| 25, chunk fallback | 483.68 μs | 486.19 μs |

Warm-eager measurements use 20 warmups per arm and six alternating AB/BA pairs of 50 calls, with synchronized wall timing; the table reports medians. Eight-token graph replay measures **195.18 → 76.34 μs** using NPU events, six alternating pairs of 100 replays. These are KDA wrapper latencies.

| Device assertion | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 2/4/8-token wrapper output and state vs direct recurrent invocation | Exact match |
| 9/25-token fallback vs original chunk wrapper | Exact match |
| Sequence lengths 3/4 padded to eight rows | Selected states, cold state, untouched slots and zero padding checked |
| Captured recurrent replay vs eager execution | Output/state match |

The same benchmark records the numerical difference between the original chunk path and the recurrent candidate:

| Token rows | Maximum absolute output difference | Maximum absolute state difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2 | 1.52587890625e−5 | 4.1216611862e−4 |
| 4 | 2.288818359375e−5 | 3.9605051279e−4 |
| 8 | 1.52587890625e−5 | 3.3286586404e−4 |

The current-commit common-reference experiment above evaluates this algorithm switch separately. Model integration, trained-model quality and end-to-end latency remain untested.

[Reproduction scripts, raw timing samples and original experiment record](https://gist.github.com/KeyanHu-git/e39282dcbfe699c4f1c977e9bd4e2bbc).

<details>
<summary>CPU test command and device reproduction</summary>

The local CPU run recorded 50 passing tests:

TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest -q \
